messages:
Maria (sales): Hey team — merchant POC asked for a single-package handoff: CAIQ, redlined DPA, SCC mapping, and a clear DSAR deletion workflow. They need it by EOD Thurs. Can we align? :eyes:
Elena (security): I can export the CAIQ and the latest SOC/Sec posture doc. Need confirmation which SCC version they want (2010 vs 2021 template?).
Maria (sales): They mentioned 'EU SCCs (current)' in the RFP, but not specific version. Assume 2021 unless legal says otherwise.
Marta (legal): Confirming — go with 2021 SCCs. I'll prepare a DPA redline focusing on data retention, subprocessors, and DSAR turnaround SLA.
Raj (eng): For the DSAR deletion workflow: we have two paths — hosted (we can trigger deletion via internal job) and private (customer-managed). Which POC environment?
Maria (sales): Hosted POC on dedicated capacity in us-west-2. They want logs retained for 30 days and user-content deletion on request.
Elena (security): Hosted will be fine. For logs, we need to ensure audit logs are retained per the retention policy and that deletion requests don't remove audit trails needed for security investigations.
Marta (legal): Exact clause I'll propose in the DPA: "We will delete Customer Data upon verified request, except for logs required for security/compliance, retained no longer than 90 days unless otherwise required by law."
Maria (sales): Can we surface a short explainer for the customer about what gets deleted vs what is retained for security? They asked for plain language.
Raj (eng): Yep — I can draft a blurb. Also note: model KV cache artifacts are ephemeral and not persisted beyond session unless customer opts into long-term storage.
Elena (security): I'll attach the CAIQ export here once ready. Also flag: subprocessors list must be current — we just added a new infra partner last week.
PSM Bot: New SIG request created: SIG-2026-045. Assigned to Elena (security) and Marta (legal). Deadline: 2026-03-26.
Marta (legal): DPA redline draft (excerpt):
```
Section 4(c) Deletion: "Provider shall, upon Customer's documented request, delete Customer Personal Data within thirty (30) days, except for data that Provider is legally required to retain or that is necessary for security incident investigation, which shall be retained no longer than ninety (90) days unless otherwise required."
```
Marta (legal): Is 30 days OK or do we want 14? Customer asked for 'as soon as possible' but we need operational buffer.
Elena (security): 30 days is safer for ops. We can offer an escalation path for urgent deletions that need faster turnaround (14 days), but only if they accept potential availability impact.
Maria (sales): Customer fine with 30 days if we provide the escalation option. They asked also for example ticket flow for DSARs.
Raj (eng): I'll add an example flow and the API call we support: POST /admin/v1/dsar/delete {"request_id": "...", "customer_id": "..."} — returns 202 and job id.
Elena (security): Also include note about backups: restores may reintroduce deleted data; we guarantee eventual deletion from backups within our restore window (max 30 days).
Marta (legal): I'll attach the redlined DPA PDF to the workspace and send to Maria for customer-facing copy.
Maria (sales): Thanks. Plan: Elena uploads CAIQ + subprocessors list; Raj uploads DSAR flow + API snippet; Marta uploads redlined DPA. I'll package and email to merchant POC. Aim to send EOD Thurs. :thumbsup:
Elena (security): CAIQ export queued — will post in ~30m.
Raj (eng): DSAR flow + sample curl posted: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/admin/v1/dsar/delete -d '{"request_id":"abc","customer_id":"cust-123"}'`
PSM Bot: SIG-2026-045 status updated: CAIQ attached.
Maria (sales): Great — once the package is ready I'll run it by legal and then send. If there are any blocker items (SCC version or subprocessor flags) ping me immediately.
Elena (security): Noted. I'll ping if subprocessors list shows anything high-risk.
Marta (legal): If customer requests a DPA clause stronger than our standard (e.g., 7-day deletion), escalate to Exec Sales.
Maria (sales): Copy. Thanks everyone.
